activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Why should you use a back-adjusted continuous futures contract rather than a simple nearest contract when backtesting a moving average system?
activeRecallQuiz.question: Why should you use a back-adjusted continuous futures contract rather than a simple nearest contract when backtesting a moving average system?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Back-adjusting eliminates artificial rollover price jumps between expiring and new contracts, preventing false moving average crossovers and indicator distortion.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Applying grounded principles prevents catastrophic losses and capital depletion.

coreTakeaways: Always evaluate underlying market assumptions before entering positions.
Separate gross theoretical payoff from real-world net profit.
Follow disciplined risk and position sizing limits on every trade.
